bib.title: A Real-World WebAgent with Planning, Long Context Understanding, and Program Synthesis

read.skipped: Reference list (chars 42994-69103) skimmed only, for lineage.

question: How can an LLM agent complete instructions on real websites despite open-ended actions, very long HTML and no HTML inductive bias?
hypothesis: Splitting web automation into planning, HTML summarization (finetuned domain-expert HTML-T5) and grounded code generation (prompted Flan-U-PaLM) beats a single prompted LLM, and local-global attention with long-span denoising captures HTML structure better.
contributions: WebAgent: integration of two modular LLMs under self-supervision for real-world web automation; domain-expert model plans and summarizes, generalist model generates executable Python programs.
HTML-T5: local-global attention encoder-decoder pre-trained with a mixture of long-span denoising on a CommonCrawl HTML corpus.
Over 50% higher success on real websites; HTML-T5 beats the prior LM agent by 18.7% on MiniWoB++ and reaches SoTA on Mind2Web.

method.summary: WebAgent loops: HTML-T5 (finetuned, seq2seq) reads instruction, sub-instruction history and raw HTML, emits the next sub-instruction and data-ref IDs of relevant snippets; frozen few-shot Flan-U-PaLM 540B turns sub-instruction plus snippet into a Selenium Python program that is executed. HTML-T5 is pre-trained on 3.41M CommonCrawl HTML examples, then finetuned on self-experience demonstrations (scripted planning/summarization plus Flan-U-PaLM-generated programs filtered by environment feedback).
method.task: instruction-following web automation on real websites (plus MiniWoB++, Mind2Web, WebSRC, Description Generation)

datasets.name: CommonCrawl HTML (100 WARC files, April 2019)
datasets.preprocessing: remove non-Unicode and alphanumeric-only documents; extract subtrees around <label> elements with a for attribute

datasets.name: Self-experience demonstrations (real-estate / social-media / map)
datasets.source: instruction templates, scripted planner, Flan-U-PaLM programs run in Selenium; critical failures filtered (execution errors, retriever errors, bad URL prefixes)
datasets.preprocessing: HTML tags such as script and meta removed, attributes id/type/value kept (Fig 2 caption)

datasets.name: MiniWoB++
datasets.size: 56 tasks, 100 eval episodes per task; 12K human demos, also 347K demos from Furuta et al. 2023
datasets.source: Liu et al. 2018; Shi et al. 2017

datasets.name: Mind2Web
datasets.preprocessing: cached candidate generation results and direct QA formulation as in Deng et al.

models.name: HTML-T5 (Base/Large/XL)
models.architecture: T5 encoder-decoder, local + transient-global attention in encoder (LongT5), dense decoder
models.init_from: PEGASUS-objective pre-trained LongT5 weights (Table 7 ablation: essential)
models.context: 4096 input / 910 output in pretraining; 16K tokens in finetuning unless stated

models.name: LongT5, Flan-LongT5, Flan-T5, WebN-T5, MindAct, Synapse

training.objective: span denoising with mean span lengths mu in {8, 64}, denoising ratio 0.15; downstream: supervised finetuning to predict next sub-instruction and data-ref snippet IDs

other.flan_longt5: finetuned LongT5 on Flan dataset for 100K iterations, best checkpoint picked

inference.samples: 20 instructions per website, one episode each (inferred: success rates are multiples of 5%); MiniWoB++ 100 episodes per task
inference.prompting: Flan-U-PaLM few-shot generic examples (select checkboxes, enter text, click options, scroll); sub-instruction is a comment in the script; WebSRC uses 5-shot
inference.retrieval: HTML-T5 predicts data-ref IDs; snippet is retrieved by those IDs; WebSRC: extract two levels up via XPath, fall back to parent, then truncate

parameters.loop_end: until end-of-episode sub-instruction predicted or maximum iterations reached (max not stated)

other.execution: Selenium WebDriver, human supervised, access rate limited

metrics.name: Score
metrics.definition: percentage of instruction attributes covered during the episode

metrics.name: Mind2Web element accuracy / operation F1 / step success rate / SR
metrics.definition: target element, operation, both per step, whole task

metrics.name: WebSRC EM / F1
metrics.definition: exact match and F1 on answers

eval.protocol: Real-website runs under human supervision; no seeds or significance tests stated; 20 episodes per site so one episode = 5 points.

limits: Modular design may add computational cost and latency (authors, Sec 5); no latency or cost numbers are given.
Flan-U-PaLM 540B makes it hard to feed back code errors into program synthesis (authors).
Real-world evaluation is costly and done under human supervision; only 3 anonymized websites and 20 instructions each, so success rates have 5-point granularity and no variance is reported.
Planning errors remain dominant: consistent long-horizon prediction without error accumulation is unsolved.
WebAgent is worse than structure-specialist baselines on KV and Table WebSRC tasks (generalist LLMs weak at tabular structure).
Finetuning hyperparameters (optimizer, lr) and max iterations of the loop are not stated; no code or weights released in this paper.
Ethics statement notes prompt-injection and misuse risk.

terms.definition: a semi-supervised approach that necessitates minimal human involvement: manually curated scripts generate planning and summarization steps, while Flan-U-PaLM generates Python programs, and domain LMs are finetuned on the result
next sub-instruction predicted conditioned on current HTML observation, instruction and history, versus open-loop planning by prompting a single LLM
